title: Last night's build failed on a unique test

ticket.subject: [FAILED] nightly dbt build: unique_stg_shop__orders_order_id
body: 03:12:09    Got 2 results, configured to fail if != 0
03:12:09  Done. PASS=6 WARN=0 ERROR=1 SKIP=4 NO-OP=0 TOTAL=11
The marts were skipped, so the revenue dashboards still show yesterday. The landing tables of last night
are in the mission's raw schema. Please find out why the test failed and fix the project so the nightly
build is green again. The test stays: it protects every join on orders downstream.

acceptance.text: The unique and not_null tests on stg_shop__orders.order_id are still there, as errors.
Your last dbt build ran every node and test, and all of them passed.
stg_shop__orders keeps one row per order: the latest delivery.

checks.sql: SELECT count(*) AS orders, count(DISTINCT order_id) AS distinct_orders, max(CASE WHEN order_id = 'SO1006' THEN payment_type END) AS so1006_payment FROM dbt_dev_uniq.stg_shop__orders
checks.fail: Orders are duplicated, missing, or not the latest delivery.

acceptance.text: fct_order_lines has each of the 16 order lines once (no line doubled by the duplicates).

checks.sql: SELECT count(*) AS order_lines, count(DISTINCT order_id || '/' || line_number) AS distinct_lines FROM dbt_dev_uniq.fct_order_lines
checks.fail: The fact is missing lines or has doubled ones.

hints: Reproduce it first: run dbt build and read which test fails and what was skipped because of it.
Look at the raw orders: which order_id values appear more than once, and what differs between the copies?
`loaded_at` says which delivery is the newer one.
DuckDB supports `qualify` with window functions such as `row_number() over (partition by ... order by ...)`.
